functions: Amount to withhold from a payment under the ATO's Schedule 1 formulas

/*  FUNCTION NAME:  PAYGWithholdingλ
    DESCRIPTION:*//**Amount to withhold from a weekly, fortnightly, monthly or quarterly payment under the ATO's Schedule 1 formulas, from a coefficient table the caller supplies*/
/*  SOURCE:         ATO, Schedule 1 - Statement of formulas for calculating amounts to be withheld (NAT 1004),
                    for payments made from 1 July 2026, published 17 June 2026, read 16 November 2026 05:48 AEDT:
                    https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/payg-withholding-schedule-1-statement-of-formulas-for-calculating-amounts-to-be-withheld
                    'Using a formula': y = a * x - b, where x is the whole dollars of weekly earnings plus 99 cents,
                    rounded to the nearest dollar, 50 cents up, with no preliminary rounding to the cent.
                    'Working out the weekly earnings': fortnightly earnings / 2; monthly earnings, plus 1 cent when
                    they end in 33 cents, * 3 / 13; quarterly earnings / 13; ignore cents, then add 99 cents. The
                    rounded weekly amount is * 2 fortnightly, * 13 / 3 rounded to the nearest dollar monthly, and
                    * 13 quarterly.
*/
PAYGWithholdingλ = LAMBDA(
//  Parameter Declaration
    [Earnings],
    [Coefficients],
    [Period],
    LET(
    //  Help
        Help,           TRIM(TEXTSPLIT(
                            "FUNCTION:      →PAYGWithholdingλ(Earnings, Coefficients, [Period])¶" &
                            "DESCRIPTION:   →Amount to withhold from a payment under the ATO's Schedule 1 formulas.¶NOTES!         →Follows Schedule 1 - Statement of formulas for calculating amounts to be¶               →withheld (NAT 1004) for payments from 1 July 2026 (read 16 November 2026):¶               →y = a * x - b on weekly earnings x, whole dollars plus 99 cents, rounded¶               →to the nearest dollar. Copy the coefficient table for the payee's scale¶               →from the ATO's current schedule; recheck it each year. Arithmetic only:¶               →it does not choose the scale, apply tax offsets, the Medicare levy¶               →adjustment or extra withholding for 53 or 27 pays, and does not do scale 4¶               →(no TFN) or working holiday makers (Schedule 15).¶" &
                            "WEBPAGE:       →https://github.com/ryanduguid/Ozzit/blob/main/docs/australian-modelling.md¶" &
                            "VERSION:       →16 Nov 2026¶" &
                            "PARAMETERS:    →¶" &
                            "Earnings       →(Required) One or more payments, with allowances subject to withholding. A blank stays blank.¶" &
                            "Coefficients   →(Required) The scale's table: 3 columns of weekly earnings 'less than', a and b, in¶" &
                            "               →ascending order. The last row is the '& over' row and is used above every bound.¶" &
                            "               →Enter a row the ATO gives no a or b for as 0 and 0.¶" &
                            "Period         →(Optional: Default = ""W"") ""W"" weekly, ""F"" fortnightly, ""M"" monthly or ""Q"" quarterly.¶" &
                            "EXAMPLES:      →¶" &
                            "→Formula (oz is assumed to be the module's name; scale 2, tax-free threshold claimed)¶" &
                            "→=oz.PAYGWithholdingλ(1333.45, {362,0,0;538,0.15,54.3462;673,0.25,108.2135;721,0.17,54.3473;865,0.179,60.8377;1282,0.3227,185.1935;2596,0.32,181.7319;3653,0.39,363.4627;3653,0.47,655.7704})¶" &
                            "→Result¶" &
                            "→245",
                            "→", "¶"
                        )),
    //  Check inputs - Omitted required arguments
        Help?,          OR( ISOMITTED( Earnings), ISOMITTED( Coefficients)),
    //  A blank Period cell is not an omitted argument, so test for both.
        Pay,            IF( ISOMITTED( Period), "W", IF( TRIM( Period & "") = "", "W", UPPER( TRIM( Period)))),
        ValidPeriod?,   AND( ROWS( Pay) = 1, COLUMNS( Pay) = 1, ISNUMBER( XMATCH( Pay, {"W", "F", "M", "Q"}, 0))),
        PeriodMessage,  "Period must be W, F, M or Q.",
    //  The row is the first whose bound is above x, so the bounds must ascend.
        Bounds,         TAKE( Coefficients, , 1),
        Ascending?,     IF( ROWS( Bounds) = 1, TRUE, AND( DROP( Bounds, 1) >= DROP( Bounds, -1))),
        ValidTable?,    AND( COLUMNS( Coefficients) = 3, AND( ISNUMBER( Coefficients)), IFERROR( Ascending?, FALSE)),
        TableMessage,   "Coefficients must be 3 columns of numbers: weekly earnings less than, a and b, with the earnings ascending.",
    //  A blank is nil and stays blank; an error passes so it shows.
        ValidEarnings?, AND( IFERROR( ISNUMBER( Earnings) * ( Earnings >= 0) + ( TRIM( Earnings & "") = ""), TRUE)),
        EarningsMessage, "PAYGWithholdingλ needs each payment to be a number of 0 or more, or blank.",
    //  Procedure
        Result,         MAP( Earnings, LAMBDA( Paid,
                            IF( TRIM( Paid & "") = "", "",
                                LET(
                                    Gross,  IF( AND( Pay = "M", ROUND( MOD( Paid, 1), 2) = 0.33), Paid + 0.01, Paid),
                                    Weekly, SWITCH( Pay, "W", Gross, "F", Gross / 2, "M", Gross * 3 / 13, "Q", Gross / 13),
                                    X,      INT( Weekly) + 0.99,
                                    Row,    IFERROR( XMATCH( TRUE, X < Bounds), ROWS( Bounds)),
                                    Y,      ROUND( INDEX( Coefficients, Row, 2) * X - INDEX( Coefficients, Row, 3), 0),
                                    SWITCH( Pay, "W", Y, "F", Y * 2, "M", ROUND( Y * 13 / 3, 0), "Q", Y * 13)
                                )
                            )
                        )),
    //  Return Result, Help, or the message
        Return,         IF( Help?, 2, IF( NOT( ValidPeriod?), 3, IF( NOT( ValidTable?), 4, IF( NOT( ValidEarnings?), 5, 1)))),
        CHOOSE( Return, Result, Help, PeriodMessage, TableMessage, EarningsMessage)
    )
);
